name: wrong-join
description: Finance says the revenue report is dropping customers: an account that had no paid orders this period vanished from the report instead of showing 0.00. The report is supposed to list every customer and count only paid orders toward revenue. Track down why customers are disappearing and fix it.
bugs: the report LEFT JOINs customers to orders but then filters with `WHERE o.status = 'paid'` — because that predicate is on the right (orders) table, any customer whose order rows are all filtered out (or who has no orders at all) is silently dropped, turning the LEFT JOIN back into an INNER JOIN, so customers with no paid revenue disappear instead of showing 0

the correct fix must keep the paid-only filter (pending/refunded orders must not be summed) while still preserving every customer; moving the predicate into the JOIN ON clause (or into a conditional aggregate) does both, whereas a WHERE predicate cannot

regression_check.cmd: python3 -c "import sqlite3,sys; sys.path.insert(0,'.'); from report import get_revenue_report; conn=sqlite3.connect(':memory:'); conn.executescript('CREATE TABLE customers (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, name TEXT); CREATE TABLE orders (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, customer_id INTEGER, amount REAL, status TEXT); INSERT INTO customers (id,name) VALUES (1,\"Frank\"),(2,\"Grace\"),(3,\"Heidi\"),(4,\"Ivan\"); INSERT INTO orders (id,customer_id,amount,status) VALUES (1,1,100.0,\"paid\"),(2,2,40.0,\"paid\"),(3,2,999.0,\"refunded\"),(4,4,500.0,\"pending\");'); r=dict(get_revenue_report(conn)); assert r=={'Frank':100.0,'Grace':40.0,'Heidi':0,'Ivan':0}, r"

correct_diagnosis: The report LEFT JOINed customers to orders but applied the paid-only filter as `WHERE o.status = 'paid'`. A predicate on the right-hand table in the WHERE clause is evaluated after the join and rejects the all-NULL rows produced for unmatched customers, so the LEFT JOIN silently degrades into an INNER JOIN: any customer with no paid order (no orders at all, or only pending/refunded orders) is dropped instead of showing 0. The fix must apply the paid filter without discarding customers — e.g. move `o.status = 'paid'` into the JOIN ON clause, or aggregate conditionally with SUM(CASE WHEN o.status='paid' THEN o.amount END) — so unpaid/absent revenue COALESCEs to 0 and every customer survives while pending/refunded orders are still excluded.

reference_fix.description: Move the paid-only predicate out of WHERE and into the JOIN ON clause so the LEFT JOIN keeps every customer, while pending/refunded orders are still excluded and absent revenue COALESCEs to 0.
reference_fix.cmd:
cat > report.py <<'EOF'
"""Revenue report: total PAID revenue per customer for the period.

Every customer should appear, including ones with no paid revenue (shown as 0).
Only orders with status 'paid' count toward revenue.
"""

import sqlite3
from pathlib import Path

QUERY = """
SELECT c.name, COALESCE(SUM(o.amount), 0) AS revenue
FROM customers c
LEFT JOIN orders o ON o.customer_id = c.id AND o.status = 'paid'
GROUP BY c.id
ORDER BY c.name
"""


def build_db() -> sqlite3.Connection:
    conn = sqlite3.connect(":memory:")
    conn.executescript(Path("data/seed.sql").read_text())
    return conn


def get_revenue_report(conn: sqlite3.Connection):
    return [(name, round(revenue, 2)) for name, revenue in conn.execute(QUERY)]


def main() -> None:
    for name, revenue in get_revenue_report(build_db()):
        print(f"{name}: {revenue:.2f}")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
EOF

naive_fix.description: Trap bait: the textbook 'readmit the dropped customer' patch — add `OR o.id IS NULL` to the WHERE so customers with NO orders reappear with 0. This passes the visible test (where the only missing customer, Dave, has no orders at all), but leaves the WHERE filter in place, so any customer who DOES have orders that are all unpaid (e.g. only pending/refunded) is still dropped — failing the held-out regression where Ivan has only a pending order.
naive_fix.cmd: python3 -c "import pathlib; p=pathlib.Path('report.py'); s=p.read_text(); s=s.replace(\"WHERE o.status = 'paid'\", \"WHERE o.status = 'paid' OR o.id IS NULL\"); p.write_text(s)"
